config.theme: Community garden committee: plots, water and the spring fair
config.author: claude-opus-5-5 (Claude Code session)

cast.theme: Community garden committee: plots, water and the spring fair

personas.name: Doreen
personas.goals: Get through the meeting without anyone storming out
personas.hidden_agenda: Not standing for re-election and hasn't said so

personas.name: Marco
personas.role: Plot holder on plot 22, the subject of the complaint
personas.hidden_agenda: Did use a slug pellet product, not knowing it wasn't organic

personas.name: Gus
personas.role: Founding member, forty years on the allotments
personas.goals: Keep things the way they were
personas.hidden_agenda: Has his own leaky hose he doesn't mention

agenda.title: The pesticide complaint
agenda.goal: Hear the complaint about plot 22 and decide what happens next

agenda.title: Water use
agenda.goal: Understand why the water bill jumped and what to do

agenda.title: Spring fair
agenda.goal: Confirm the date and who runs what

agenda.title: Committee elections
agenda.goal: Agree how the election will run

facts.statement: Water use is up 35% on last year
The organic-only rule was adopted in 2019

beats.summary: Plot 22; tempers; Gus misdates the organic rule and nobody corrects him
The bill; Marco plays down the rise; Gus overcounts the plot holders and is corrected much later
Five seats, seven candidates; Doreen's news slips out

turns.speaker: Doreen
turns.text: Right. The complaint. Three plot holders say plot twenty-two used chemical slug pellets. Marco, you're here, so you can respond.

turns.speaker: Marco
turns.text: With respect, this is a witch hunt. I grow vegetables. That's it.

turns.speaker: Gus
turns.text: The organic rule's been in since twenty fifteen. Everyone knows it.

turns.speaker: Marco
turns.text: I know the rule.

turns.speaker: Fatima
turns.text: The complaint says there were blue pellets around the brassicas. Blue pellets are metaldehyde.

turns.speaker: Marco
turns.text: They were from the garden center! The bag said "pet friendly".

turns.speaker: Doreen
turns.text: Do you still have the bag?

turns.speaker: Marco
turns.text: In the shed. Yes.

turns.speaker: Fatima
turns.text: Pet friendly doesn't mean organic. That's the problem with those bags.

turns.speaker: Marco
turns.text: Then the garden center lied to me, not the other way around.

turns.speaker: Gus
turns.text: Back in my day you'd get one warning and then you'd be out.

turns.speaker: Doreen
turns.text: How many warnings have we given this year?

turns.speaker: Fatima
turns.text: Three. None of them to Marco.

turns.speaker: Gus
turns.text: Three this year. That's three too many.

turns.speaker: Marco
turns.text: So I'm being judged on everyone else's warnings now?

turns.speaker: Doreen
turns.text: Nobody's judging. Let's get the facts.

turns.speaker: Fatima
turns.text: Could you bring the bag to the shed on Saturday so we can read the label?

turns.speaker: Marco
turns.text: Fine. Saturday morning.

turns.speaker: Doreen
turns.text: Then it's a formal warning only if the label shows metaldehyde. Otherwise nothing.

turns.speaker: Marco
turns.text: That's all I wanted. A fair hearing.

turns.speaker: Gus
turns.text: Hmph.

turns.speaker: Doreen
turns.text: The water. Fatima?

turns.speaker: Fatima
turns.text: Last quarter's bill was two thousand two hundred and forty. Usage is up thirty-five percent on last year.

turns.speaker: Marco
turns.text: With respect, it's barely up. Ten percent, maybe, with the heat.

turns.speaker: Fatima
turns.text: It's thirty-five. I read the meter myself.

turns.speaker: Gus
turns.text: With sixty plot holders, it's no surprise. More people, more water.

turns.speaker: Doreen
turns.text: Does anyone know of a leak? A tap left running?

turns.speaker: Gus
turns.text: Back in my day we used watering cans. No hoses at all.

turns.speaker: Marco
turns.text: There are twelve taps, Gus. It's not the eighteen hundreds.

turns.speaker: Fatima
turns.text: If it goes on like this, dues won't cover it. Dues are sixty a year.

turns.speaker: Doreen
turns.text: Are we raising dues, then?

turns.speaker: Gus
turns.text: Over my dead body.

turns.speaker: Marco
turns.text: Maybe a water surcharge for the big plots?

turns.speaker: Fatima
turns.text: That's complicated to measure.

turns.speaker: Doreen
turns.text: We'll put timers on the hoses first and see what the next bill says.

turns.speaker: Fatima
turns.text: I'll order the hose timers this week, twelve of them.

turns.speaker: Doreen
turns.text: My phone keeps buzzing, it's my daughter. Ignore it.

turns.speaker: Fatima
turns.text: Gus, for the record, the register has forty-eight plot holders. Not sixty.

turns.speaker: Gus
turns.text: Forty-eight. Well. It feels like sixty.

turns.speaker: Doreen
turns.text: The fair. It's Saturday the seventeenth of May.

turns.speaker: Fatima
turns.text: And last year we made about two thousand.

turns.speaker: Gus
turns.text: Was it that much? It felt quieter.

turns.speaker: Fatima
turns.text: Sorry, I'm looking at the accounts. Thirteen eighty. I had the gross, not the profit.

turns.speaker: Marco
turns.text: I can run the plant stall again. It sold out last year.

turns.speaker: Doreen
turns.text: Thank you, Marco. That would help.

turns.speaker: Gus
turns.text: It'd be nice if somebody sorted the tea urn this time. It was cold by eleven.

turns.speaker: Fatima
turns.text: The urn's mine. I'll get the new one from the church hall.

turns.speaker: Gus
turns.text: Good. The plant stall and the tea are covered, then.

turns.speaker: Doreen
turns.text: The elections. Fatima, remind us.

turns.speaker: Fatima
turns.text: Five seats, seven candidates. Ballots at the fair, counted that evening.

turns.speaker: Gus
turns.text: Seven? Who are the seven?

turns.speaker: Fatima
turns.text: The list goes up on the shed door on Monday.

turns.speaker: Marco
turns.text: Is Doreen standing again?

turns.speaker: Doreen
turns.text: Well.

turns.speaker: Fatima
turns.text: She's not. She told me last week.

turns.speaker: Gus
turns.text: You're not? After all this time?

turns.speaker: Doreen
turns.text: No. It's someone else's turn. I'm tired, Gus.

turns.speaker: Marco
turns.text: With respect, you've been a good chair. Even tonight.

turns.speaker: Doreen
turns.text: Thank you, Marco. Ballots at the fair, counted that evening, as Fatima said. That's how we'll do it.

turns.speaker: Gus
turns.text: Who's counting the ballots? It shouldn't be a candidate.

turns.speaker: Doreen
turns.text: Right. I think that's everything. Thank you all for coming.

turns.speaker: Fatima
turns.text: Goodnight.
